name: Mississippi

default_limits.basis: Miss. Code § 63-3-501: 65 mph max on state highways unless otherwise provided; Transportation Commission may raise Interstates and 4+ lane controlled-access roads to 70 (posted); toll roads up to 80. No statewide unposted residential/urban default found; local authorities set those (posted).

fine.notes: Speeding is a misdemeanor: 1st conviction up to $100 fine or up to 10 days jail (§ 63-9-11). Amount set by court/local schedule. State assessments (~$91+) are added on top.

court_costs.notes: $91 mandatory state assessments (§ 99-19-73(1) $90.50 + $0.50). Plus trauma fee $10/$20/$30 for 10-20/20-30/30+ over, $10 if Highway Patrol ticket or up to $10 local, small optional local fees, and municipal court costs up to $50.

points.notes: No points system; convictions go on driving record. Secondary source.

zones.work_zone: Higher fines in highway work zones (§ 63-3-516): reported up to $250 1st, $500 2nd+ (secondary source).
zones.school_zone: Posted school-zone limits apply; no statewide extra-fine amount verified.

court.reason: No statewide speed threshold for mandatory court found; fines are at the court's discretion.

arrest.offense: Reckless driving (general; no speed number in statute)

notes: No speed makes it automatically reckless. Reckless: 1st $5-$100 fine; 2nd+ up to 10 days jail/$500 (secondary sources; statute text not read). Every speeding ticket is technically a misdemeanor (up to 10 days jail, § 63-9-11 text read via 2002 bill). Bills to raise limits to 70/75 failed in 2025 and stalled in 2026.
